current.text: He is a projected starter for Cleveland next to Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
His usage, shot attempts, free throw attempts and scoring dropped after he joined Cleveland. He averaged under 20 points there and plays more as a distributor next to Mitchell, Mobley and Watson.
Over his last six games in Cleveland he played about 33 minutes with a usage of about 24 to 25. His assists and FG% dropped in that stretch.
Experts do not expect the usage drop to reverse. He probably will not repeat 35 minutes a night or last season's finish.
He is no longer a round two pick. Fair value is about picks 28 to 40 in category leagues, the end of round three in a 12-team league. Pick 35 feels about right.
ESPN's rank of 23 to 25 and his round two ADP are too high. A Yahoo rank of about 30 is fine for category leagues.
He went for 24 USD in an auction mock draft.
His auction value is all over the place. The expected price is in the low to mid 20s USD.
Cleveland's second unit has no clear point guard, so Harden and Mitchell may stagger their minutes.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With a March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and 2 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. Finals week, starting March 22, has only two games.
The two-game finals week lowers his value.
Cleveland has no current injury concerns.

durable.text: He is still an elite assist source, and his assists keep their value.
Assists and high-volume FT% are his league-outlier strengths. Turnovers are a league-outlier weakness, and his FG% is weak for a guard.
He gets to the free throw line less than he used to. His FG% and two-point percentage have fallen, and he no longer adds much in steals and blocks.
He is starting the end-of-career decline and showed his age last season.
He is considered a durable player.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues. He finished 13th in categories and 19th in points last season. The expert range is picks 28 to 40 in categories and 35 to 50 in points.

note: He cost 42 USD in our league last season, but experts now price him in the low to mid 20s USD (a mock went for 24). The market is split: Yahoo's average cost is 19.4 USD and ESPN's is 28.0, against a 29 USD value on both. He suits punt FG% and punt TO builds that want elite assists and FT%. The two-game finals week hurts him. Early in the season, check whether he plays more than 33 minutes and how much he staggers with Mitchell.
